tagline: The model can become a measure for its supposed original
definition: An image, likeness, or representation; in some modern theoretical uses, especially Baudrillard's, a simulation whose relation to an original becomes unstable, displaced, or no longer sufficient to explain its social reality.
etymology: From Latin simulacrum, likeness, image, or representation, related to simulare, to make like; later theories transform rather than erase the ordinary meaning.

sections.heading: The ordinary likeness
sections.text: A simulacrum can simply be an image, likeness, or representation. That broad historical sense remains relevant even when later theory gives the word more specialized force. A statue or replica need not immediately exemplify every philosophical account associated with the term merely because it resembles another thing.

sections.heading: The authority can reverse
sections.text: A souvenir village might become the standard by which visitors judge the actual settlement. Residents then alter buildings to match the idealized model. Representation is no longer only following its supposed original; it helps organize expectations and behavior that transform the reality whose authenticity it appears to certify.

sections.heading: Baudrillard's particular challenge
sections.text: Baudrillard investigates signs and simulations whose relation to an original becomes unstable or insufficient to explain their social reality. His account is more demanding than announcing that modern things are fake. Different philosophers use simulacrum differently, so attribution and conceptual setting matter when explaining what kind of displacement is claimed.

sections.heading: Artificial is not automatically false
sections.text: A model can be explicitly artificial and still provide reliable knowledge. A replica can preserve access to a fragile object. The critical question concerns how representations acquire authority, circulate, and organize experience, rather than whether an object is manufactured or whether its materials happen to be authentically old.

literary: The village rebuilt itself to resemble the souvenir sold at its station, until the miniature's painted shutters became the measure of authenticity and the old crooked windows apologized for being real.
art_caption: An enclosed miniature sends its pattern outward to larger houses: representation begins to prescribe the reality it appears to imitate.
